title: Utility Order for Entergy Louisiana, LLC, ex parte. — Order No. U-37812 certifies the Babel - Webre 500kV Project pursuant to General Order dated September 10, 2024 (Transmission Siting Order) subject to the conditions contained therein. This matter was considered at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                   ORDER NUMBER U-37812

                         ENTERGY LOUISIANA, LLC, EX PARTE.

Docket No. U-37812, In re: Application for certification of the Babel - Webre 500kV
transmission project in accordance with General Order dated September 10, 2024 (R-36199).

               (Decided at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                              ORDER


I.     Overview

       On December 23, 2025, Entergy Louisiana, LLC (“ELL” or the “Company”) filed an

Application with the Commission (the “Application”) seeking certification by the LPSC that the

public convenience and necessity would be served by the completion and siting of a new 147-mile

500kV transmission line and related facilities extending generally between the Babel substation,

located 4 miles into Texas from the Louisiana border, and the Webre substation near Rosedale

Louisiana, west of Baton Rouge, together with associated transmission infrastructure and

upgrades. As proposed, the Project is intended to go into service in August 2029 and create an

additional east-west 500kV transmission path across south Louisiana. The Project is also intended

to function as part of the broader regional Extra High Voltage (“EHV”) transmission backbone

connecting southeast Texas, southwest Louisiana, and southeast Louisiana. Entergy Texas, Inc.

(“Entergy Texas” or “ETI”) is separately advancing a related transmission reinforcement project

consisting of a new Babel 500kV Switching Station and 145 miles of 500kV transmissions line in

Texas intended to interconnect with and strengthen the broader transfer capability associated with

the proposed Babel-Webre facilities. Babel-Webre is projected to cost about $1.238 billion. This

is a “Class 3” cost estimate which can be up to 20 percent below or 30 percent above the estimated

amount,



       Babel-Webre will serve several purposes. First, absent the project NERC reliability

standards may be implicated due to contingency-related overload and reliability concerns. In

addition, the project will be part of a regional EHV transmission backbone connecting southeast

Texas, southwest Louisiana, and southeast Louisiana. It is intended to improve east-west transfer

capability, operational flexibility, import capability, and reliability across interconnected portions

of south Louisiana and southeast Texas. It has already been approved by the Midcontinent

                                                                                 Order No. U-37812
                                                                                            Page 1
 Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”). It will improve operational flexibility during

stressed conditions and improve reliability during hurricanes and other major outage events.



        Southern Renewable Energy Association (“SREA”), Alliance for Affordable Energy

(“Alliance”), and Louisiana Energy Users Group (“LEUG”). and the Union of Concerned

Scientists (“UCS”) all intervened in this proceeding. On February 5, 2026, the LEUG filed a

Statement of Objection and on February 10, 2026, the LPSC Staff filed an Objection Without

Prejudice - both in accordance with the requirements set forth in the General Order dated

September 10, 2024 in Docket No. R-36199 ("2024 Siting Order").1 Together the Applicant, Staff

and Intervenors will be referred to as the “Parties”.



        After the completion of discovery, on May 29, 2026, the LPSC Staff filed the Direct

Testimony of R. Lane Sisung and the Direct Testimony of John A. Chapman. On that same date,

SREA filed the Direct Testimony of Michael Goggin. Those testimonies recommended that the

record was sufficient for the Commission to approve the Babel-Webre Project.



        After testimony was filed, the parties began settlement discussions, and on August 27, 2026

the Parties entered into an “Uncontested Stipulated Settlement Agreement”. On September 15,

2026, ELL, Staff, and SREA filed a “Joint Motion to Schedule Uncontested Stipulation Hearing”.

That Joint Motion included the Uncontested Stipulated Settlement Agreement, and it included

testimony in support of the settlement by ELL witness Ryan D. Jones, Staff witness R. Lane

Sisung, and SREA witness Michael Goggin. The Settlement was supported or not opposed by all

Parties to this proceeding. On September 30,2026, a stipulation hearing was held before an

Administrative Law Judge, who filed a report that same date. That report determined that there

were no disputed issues requiring a recommendation of the ALJ. The matter was included on the

agenda of the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session for Commission consideration.




1 LPSC General Order dated September 10, 2024, In re: Review and Possible Modification of the Commission’s

General Order dated October 10, 2013 Governing Transmission Certification and General Siting in Docket No. R-
36199.

                                                                                        Order No. U-37812
                                                                                                   Page 2
 II.    COMMISSION JURISDICTION

       The Commission's authority and jurisdiction are specifically set forth in Article IV Section

21 of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974, which sets forth in pertinent part:

               The Commission shall regulate all common carriers and public
               utilities and shall have such other regulatory authority as provided
               by law. It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations and
               procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and perform
               other duties as provided by law.

III.   STIPULATED SETTLEMENT

1.     Under the Commission’s General Order dated September 24, 2024 in Docket No. R-36199
(the “2024 Siting Order”), the construction, completion, and siting of the components of the
Louisiana portion of the Babel – Webre 500kV Project will serve the public convenience and
necessity and be in the public interest and are therefore approved, including principally the
following Project components:


       a.      the construction of a new approximately 147-mile 500kV transmission line in south
       Louisiana extending from the reconstructed Webre substation to the Texas border (Sabine
       River); and


       b.      the reconstruction of the Webre 500kV Switching Station;


And, further, undertaking the construction of the Project components would therefore be prudent,
serves the public convenience and necessity, and meets the conditions of certification in
accordance with the 2024 Siting Order and other applicable Commission orders.


2.     The generalized siting of the Babel – Webre 500kV Project is appropriate, and its
construction is a reasonable and cost-effective solution to provide reliable electric service to the
anticipated load growth in southeast Louisiana and the Amite South region, and to maintain
compliance with applicable federal regulations as the Company serves a new large load customer
in northeast Louisiana, as described in the Company’s Application.


3.     The actual retail revenue requirement associated with the prudently incurred costs of the
Babel – Webre 500kV Project, an estimate of which is provided by Company witness Ryan Jones
in his Direct Testimony in support of the Application, is deemed eligible for recovery by the
Company at the time that the components of the Babel – Webre 500kV Project are placed in service
through the Company’s Formula Rate Plan (“FRP”) to the extent the Company remains subject to
one, or in the alternative where there is no FRP, the Commission authorizes the creation of a
regulatory asset which shall accrue carrying charges on the net of tax balance at the then-effective
weighted average cost of capital until such time that the costs can be reflected in rates.




                                                                                Order No. U-37812
                                                                                           Page 3
 4.     The Commission approval should in no manner serve as a determination of the prudence
of the final costs of the Babel – Webre 500kV Project. The Company has an ongoing obligation to
prudently manage the Babel – Webre 500kV Project, including but not limited to ongoing
construction and costs and whether to continue the investment. The certification of the Babel –
Webre 500kV Project is not a determination of prudence of the final costs of the Project but rather
only a determination that the prudently incurred costs of the project are eligible for recovery from
customers. The estimates provided in the Application are only current Class 3 estimates, and the
final costs will be submitted in the normal ratemaking process.


5.     ELL will file with the Commission semi-annual reports pursuant to and consistent with the
terms of Section VI (Construction Reporting) of the Commission’s 2024 Siting Order, and such
construction reporting requirements shall apply to all components of the Project (i.e.,the Switching
Station Components, Right of Way Components, and Proposed Transmission Facilities) including
those components that may or may not individually qualify for exemption from certification, or
fall outside of the Commission’s consideration under the 2024 Siting Order.


6.     The Uncontested Settlement as a whole is reasonable, should be approved by the
Commission, and is in the public interest.


7.     This Uncontested Settlement will be effective and enforceable upon approval by the
Commission. The LPSC Staff, the Company, SREA, LEUG, the Alliance, and UCS agree to
promptly file this Uncontested Settlement and to cooperate and take reasonable steps to request
the approval of this Uncontested Settlement by the Commission.


8.     Except as expressly stated herein, this Uncontested Settlement shall have no precedential
effect in any other proceedings involving issues similar to those resolved herein and shall be
without prejudice to the right of any party to take any position on any such similar issues in future
proceedings, including FRP proceedings, base rate proceedings, rulemakings, or in other
regulatory proceedings or appeals therefrom. Other than in a proceeding to approve, implement,
administer, or enforce a requirement of this Uncontested Settlement, the Uncontested Settlement
shall not be admissible in evidence against either the Staff, ELL, SREA, LEUG, the Alliance, or
UCS, and the terms of this Uncontested Settlement may not be used as an admission of any sort in
any proceeding whatsoever except to approve or enforce the terms of this Uncontested Settlement.
Nothing stated herein is intended to prohibit parties from continuing to cite to final Orders of the
Commission, which Orders are the best evidence of their meaning and evidentiary or precedential
value (if any).

 IV. COMMISSION CONSIDERATION

       This matter was considered by the Commission at its October 22, 2026 Business and

Executive Session.     After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by

Commissioner Lewis, and unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to accept the Uncontested

Stipulated Settlement filed into the record on September 15, 2026.

IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED THAT:

       1. The Uncontested Stipulated Settlement filed into the record on September 15, 2026 is
          accepted; and,

       2. This order is effective immediately.


BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
November 23, 2026
